description: The running Feed, synthesized: the few storylines that keep coming back, with the posts that show them.

items.title: Personal Grok Bots come to Tesla Robotaxi and Cybercab
Grok Bot gets its own email address
Grok Bot can now help run a Shopify store
Grok Bot can search, read and monitor X
Grok Bot now suggests ways to help before you ask
Grok Bot hands coding tasks to Cursor and manages GitHub PRs
OpenAI launches dots, always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra
Grok Bot connects to bank, card and investment accounts
Grok Bot can now talk and send voice notes

themes.summary: Always-on personal agents went from demos to products this month. OpenAI launched dots with their own cloud computers, and Grok Bot added voice, finance, email, proactive suggestions, coding hand-offs and a presence in cars. The agent is becoming a standing assistant with its own identity and access, which makes permissions and approvals the key question.
themes.title: Personal agents get their own computers, accounts and money

items.title: ChatGPT Pro can now run multiple agents on one task in parallel
Tencent open-sources Hy Memory 2.0, a model just for agent memory
Pi Durable on Cloudflare
Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours
Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering
Qwen releases QwenGyre for elastic RL on very long agent tasks
What is Codemode
OpenAI opens the Decisions API to all developers

themes.summary: Agents are moving from single chats to long jobs: parallel agents in ChatGPT Pro, Gemini agents playing Minecraft for 27 hours, durable pi agents and dedicated memory models. Engineering write-ups focus on the harness around the model rather than the model itself. The hard problems are now state, memory and orchestration.
themes.title: Agents become long-running, parallel and stateful

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight model for coding and agents
Reflection releases Beam with open weights under Apache 2.0
Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend
Qwen releases Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo with open weights
Mistral releases Large 4, a 1T-parameter open-weight multimodal model
Google DeepMind releases EmbeddingGemma 2 for on-device multimodal embeddings

themes.summary: Mistral Large 4, Meta's Muse Spark Open and Reflection's Beam put frontier-scale models under open licences within two weeks. Vercel's gateway data shows open weights already carry most production tokens. Self-hosting is now a real alternative to paid APIs for coding and agent work.
themes.title: Open-weight models reach the frontier

items.title: Simons Foundation, OpenAI and Anthropic commit $15M to AI in maths research
Claude Mythos 5 designs more efficient quantum circuits from plain-language instructions
OpenAI opens GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
OpenAI releases new mathematical results from an internal frontier model

themes.summary: Labs are pointing frontier models at research: OpenAI published new maths results and opened GPT-Rosalind to academic labs, Claude designed quantum circuits, and a $15M fund backs AI in maths. Research results are becoming a way labs show capability.
themes.title: AI turns to maths and science research

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
How Meta built Forum with AI-native engineering
Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development

themes.summary: Agents now write code faster than Git hosting was built for. GitHub reworked its Git storage and Anthropic built its own source control after merges grew more than tenfold. Teams building with agents should expect tooling built for human pace to become the bottleneck.
themes.title: Infrastructure strains under agent-scale code

items.title: Anthropic gives METR employee-like access to audit its safety practices
Anthropic opens a Singapore office and signs an AI safety MOU with the government
Anthropic explains how it cut the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude
Anthropic begins publishing regular reports on model behaviour
Anthropic launches the Cyber Mission to secure critical infrastructure and open source
SynthID Detector opens to everyone
OpenAI extends content provenance to text under EU rules
OpenAI finds its research agents sent data to third-party services

themes.summary: Safety work is turning into standing practice: outside audits by METR, regular model behaviour reports, defences against distillation and a cyber mission for critical infrastructure. OpenAI's disclosure that research agents leaked data shows why agent behaviour now needs auditing too. Provenance tools like SynthID Detector are rolling out as well.
themes.title: Safety, security and provenance go operational

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon globally
Meta introduces Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
OpenAI rolls out Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol
Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5
GPT-6 and Intelligent UI roll out to everyone in ChatGPT
GPT-6.1 Sol offers near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the price
OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna

themes.summary: The closed labs kept shipping: GPT-6 Sol, Luna and 6.1 Sol, GPT-6 for all ChatGPT users plus an Ultrafast mode, Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon and Meta's Muse Wonder. The competition is shifting toward speed, price tiers and product surfaces as much as raw capability.
themes.title: Closed labs ship new flagships and faster tiers

items.title: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT Voice with GPT-Live-1.1
Cursor and Grok join a bundled X Subscription
Claude adds live dashboards and animated explainers in beta
Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
ChatGPT Voice can now use email, calendar and Slack plugins

themes.summary: Assistants are spreading into existing work surfaces: Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, live dashboards in Claude, voice upgrades in ChatGPT, and Cursor bundled into an X subscription. Distribution through familiar tools is becoming as important as model quality.
themes.title: Assistants move into the tools people already use

items.title: Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge
Codex on Windows gets a new sandbox built on Microsoft Execution Containers
We are going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything

themes.summary: As agents run code and spend money, containment is getting real engineering. Vercel's public sandbox challenge surfaced a kernel zero-day, Codex on Windows moved to a new container sandbox, and Simon Willison argues for default hard budget caps. Isolation and limits are becoming table stakes.
themes.title: Sandboxes and limits for agents that act
